title: Canonical BSP variant B conformance: the standard template verifies on the emulator

target.what: A project generated by tools/picocalc.py new, built for the recommended default display variant

build.note: The no-stored-UF2 rule governs artefacts handed to the device; the emulator reads a BIN and the build already emits one. Nothing is committed here but the identity.

primary_source_findings.shift_engine: Two instructions: 'out pins, 1 side 0' presents a MOSI bit with SCK low, 'nop side 1' raises SCK. Mode 0, MSB first, autopull at 8 bits.
primary_source_findings.wiring: SCK GP10 and MOSI GP11 driven by PIO0; CS GP13, DC GP14 and RESET GP15 driven by the CPU through SIO
primary_source_findings.transfer_contract: COLMOD 0x65, RGB565 two bytes per pixel, clkdiv 2.00, window at most 160x160, pixels in units of 160
primary_source_findings.readback: The GRAM readback parks the PIO program and bit-bangs SCK/MOSI/MISO from SIO, following the life capture procedure

generic_hook.why: A PIO program drives pins directly, so a device on the far end is only observable by watching the pads. The SPI hook added at Gate 2 cannot see this traffic at all.

board_model.detail: Reassembles bytes from rising SCK edges while CS is asserted, forwards the CPU-driven control lines, and drives MISO for readback. Feeds the same St7365p model variant A uses.
board_model.separation: The two transports remain separate implementations, as the plan requires. Only the panel model and framebuffer are shared, because the display and its command set are the same part either way.

defects_fixed.symptom: The template hung in write_command polling PIO0 FDEBUG; display init never completed.
defects_fixed.cause: FDEBUG.TXSTALL was readable and write-1-to-clear but nothing ever set it. The BSP's wait-idle helper clears the bit, pushes a transfer, and waits for it to come back.
defects_fixed.why_fstat_is_not_enough: FSTAT.TXEMPTY goes true while the last word is still being shifted out, so it cannot mean end-of-transfer. TXSTALL means the shift engine ran dry, which is the question the firmware is actually asking.
defects_fixed.fix: PioBlock latches TXSTALL for any state machine stalled on an empty TX FIFO.

defects_fixed.symptom: Bytes decoded, but with wrong values: COLMOD read back as 0x66 when 0x65 was sent.
defects_fixed.cause: has_pin_watching_device only checked for PSRAM, so attaching a pin device did not switch the serial loop to per-cycle GPIO observation and SCK edges were lost between quantum boundaries.
defects_fixed.fix: The predicate now includes attached pin devices.

defects_fixed.symptom: Every pixel misread; readback of white returned 0xf8fc rather than 0xffff.
defects_fixed.cause: COLMOD was matched against 0x55 and 0x66 only. The register holds two independent widths -- RGB (DPI) interface in bits [6:4] and MCU (DBI) interface in bits [2:0] -- and everything here arrives over the MCU interface. The BSP writes 0x65 (18-bit RGB, 16-bit MCU), which was treated as unknown, leaving the previous format in force.
defects_fixed.fix: Decode the DBI field alone. RAMRD gains the matching width, two bytes per pixel rather than three.

defects_fixed.symptom: Readback shifted by one byte: 0x00f8 where 0xffff was written.
defects_fixed.cause: The panel always emits a dummy byte after RAMRD, but where it lands depends on the transport. Variant A's SPI hook answers within the same transfer; a bit-level full-duplex wire is already a byte behind, so counting the dummy again pushed pixel data a byte late.
defects_fixed.fix: St7365p::set_ramrd_dummy makes the dummy optional; the PIO wire disables it.

boot_line.evidence: [PICOCALC][BOOT] bsp=0.8.8 app=0.8.4-b-pio-rgb565-default variant=pio-rgb565, followed by clock status=ok target_khz=250000 actual_khz=250000

lcd_verify_app_status.evidence: [PICOCALC][LCD][VERIFY] app_status=pass after solid-fill and known-pattern stages, every stage reporting mismatches=0

gram_readback.evidence: RAMRD through the SIO bit-bang path returned the written values for all five fill colours and the pattern samples; lcd.ramrd counted 6 read sequences.

visual.evidence: The framebuffer shows the BSP smoke pattern exactly as specified: green top band, blue bottom band, white frame, and red/green/blue blocks. Sol read the PNG on 2026-08-04.

unsupported_declared_not_swallowed.evidence: SPI0 SD is listed as unsupported in capability.json; the run stops with the SD smoke at component=init status=begin rather than silently reporting success.

determinism.evidence: report.json, uart.log and fb.png are byte-identical across three runs.

variant_a_unaffected.evidence: The Gate 2 golden framebuffer hash cb4251497590686c3c8665287b15fe80bb20ba7b6f287779e3850e5a1e0cc966 is unchanged.

known_limitations: SPI0 SD is not modelled, so the template's SD smoke stalls at init. Nothing after it in the boot sequence -- the keyboard event loop in particular -- has been exercised through this path yet.

The BSP's own PSRAM driver reports verify failures under this configuration. It uses fudge=0 at clkdiv 2.00, where the official sample uses fudge=true at clkdiv 1.00, and the PSRAM model's read-output delay was calibrated for the latter at Gate 3. The delay is a property of the transfer timing, not of the chip alone, and making one model serve both settings is open work.
Timing is not calibrated against silicon; correlation with the device is Milestone 4.
